 Safety warning issued for hundreds of thousands of pressure cookers nationwide
 Prev 
 Next 
 The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) is warning consumers to immediately stop using 6-quart Power Quick Pot pressure cookers, model Y6D-36, due to a burn hazard. (Scripps News) 
 By: 
 Kelly Broderick 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) is warning consumers to immediately stop using 6-quart Power Quick Pot pressure cookers, model Y6D-36, due to a burn hazard.
 There have been 24 reports of the pressure cookers unexpectedly expelling hot contents, resulting in serious burn injuries.
 RECENT RECALL |  Recall issued for this mango brand due to possible Salmonella contamination 
 According to officials, the lid can open while the cooker is pressurized. Consumers are urged to stop using the product and dispose of it.
 The pressure cookers have a black pressure lid, button controls and a digital temperature and function display. "Power Quick Pot" is printed on the front, and the model number appears on a label on the back of the unit.
 They were sold nationwide between July 2018 and November 2023 for between $44 and $160.
 MORE RECALLS |  FDA elevates egg recall to highest risk level over salmonella concerns 
 The CPSC says the importer, Tristar Products Inc. of Altamonte Springs, Florida, has refused to recall the products or offer a remedy to consumers.
 While there is no official recall, the CPSC estimates that about 393,000 units are affected.
